serp_observations: Scribd dominates any query containing 'pdf' or 'free download' (4-6 of 10 results). These are user-uploaded, login-gated, uncurated, and mostly English-only.

englishwale.com and spokenenglishtips.com did NOT appear for any query; Spoken English Guru/EnglishWale content surfaces only as pirated Scribd/Teachmint PDFs. Searching their names directly returned auto-generated spam pages (maidsafe.net, strikolith.com, onlinenic.com blogs with 176xxxxxxx timestamps), which indicates low-quality competition in the Hindi cluster.

Hindi-meaning cluster is owned by small blogs: talkdrill.com (3 URLs, strongest, app competitor), engfusionbharat.com (1 URL ranking for 9+ queries, free PDF, inflated counts), speaknowenglish.com (2023, paid PDFs), mrmrsenglish.com, englishtak.com, kamalshukla.com, hindimediumhelp.blogspot.com.
English-only '100 sentences' cluster is a different SERP: speakshark, englishpartner, fluentra, loora, grammareco, planetspark, leverageedu. SpeakX should not chase this with the same page.
Only two ranking pages carry a 'when to use' column (talkdrill, speakshark); SpeakX already has it.

No ranking page offers a free, direct, Hindi-included, exactly-100 PDF. engfusionbharat's is free but claims 5000 and has garbled Hindi; talkdrill's is a 300-sentence lead-magnet; speaknowenglish's are paid; grammareco's is a .docx without Hindi.
Year in title ('(2026)') is used by talkdrill, engfusionbharat, planetspark, speakshark ('Updated July 27, 2026').

metadata_recommendation.justification: The page ranks #1 for '100 daily use english sentences with hindi meaning pdf' on 16 impressions WITHOUT a PDF or the word 'pdf' on the page, which signals weak competition rather than a fragile win. The verified head term (590/mo) uses the word order 'daily use english sentences' + 'pdf'; the current title uses 'Simple English Sentences for Daily Use' and omits 'pdf' and the word 'meaning', so it is not an exact-phrase match for either the head term or the GSC query. Retaining '100' and 'Hindi Meaning' preserves the existing long-tail match; adding 'Daily Use' word order and 'PDF' targets the head term. Risk is limited to 2 clicks/month; expected upside is the 590/mo head term plus the pdf/download cluster. Do the title/meta/H1 change in the same deploy as the real PDF so the page can satisfy the intent it claims. Keep 'simple English sentences for daily use' in the intro paragraph and one H2 to retain that secondary cluster. Monitor GSC for 4-6 weeks; revert title only if impressions for the GSC query fall to zero.
